---
title: "Maths"
subtitle: "Write every equation in Typst syntax."
description: "The math: typst takeover, which formats it reaches, Typst maths syntax, and the block form that works everywhere."
# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine
# detection, which then selects Jupyter and fails for want of a kernel. The
# extension compiles those blocks itself, so the page needs no engine.
engine: markdown
extensions:
  typst-render:
    math: typst
---

Quarto reads `$...$` and `$$...$$` as LaTeX.
`math: typst` tells the extension to read them as Typst instead, so one syntax writes every equation of the document:

```yaml
extensions:
  typst-render:
    math: typst
```

This page sets that option in its own front matter, so every equation below is Typst.

## Where the takeover applies

| Output | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| HTML, Reveal.js, and EPUB | Each equation is compiled to native MathML, so it stays selectable text and scales with the text around it. Typst 0.15 or later is needed. |
| Typst | Each equation passes through unchanged, and the Typst compiler reads it directly. |
| PDF, Word, and the rest | Quarto's own renderer stays in place, so the equations are read as LaTeX. |

: What each output does with `math: typst`. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

On an older Typst the extension writes a warning and leaves the HTML equations to Quarto.
For a document that must produce PDF or Word as well, use the block form in [Equations that work everywhere](#equations-that-work-everywhere).

::: {.callout-important}
`math` is a global option.
Set it under `extensions.typst-render` in the document or the project, never on a block.
:::

## Inline and display

```markdown
The sum $f(x) = sum_(i=0)^n x_i$ sits in the sentence.

$$
e^(i pi) + 1 = 0
$$
```

The sum $f(x) = sum_(i=0)^n x_i$ sits in the sentence.

$$
e^(i pi) + 1 = 0

## Numbering and cross-references

The takeover runs after Quarto has numbered the equations, so labels and `@eq-` references keep working:

```markdown
$$
integral_0^1 x^2 dif x = 1/3
$$ {#eq-integral}

See @eq-integral.
```

$$
integral_0^1 x^2 dif x = 1/3
$$ {#eq-integral}

See @eq-integral.

## Typst maths syntax

Typst writes maths with words and parentheses rather than backslashes.
The most common differences:

| LaTeX | Typst |
| --- | --- |
| `\frac{a}{b}` | `a/b` |
| `\sum_{i=0}^{n}` | `sum_(i=0)^n` |
| `\int_0^1 x^2\,dx` | `integral_0^1 x^2 dif x` |
| `\alpha \beta \gamma` | `alpha beta gamma` |
| `\sqrt{x}` | `sqrt(x)` |
| `\mathbf{v}` | `bold(v)` |
| `\begin{matrix}` | `mat(...)` |
| `\begin{cases}` | `cases(...)` |

: The same maths in both syntaxes. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[50,50]"}

A matrix:

```markdown
$$
A = mat(1, 2; 3, 4)
$$
```

$$
A = mat(1, 2; 3, 4)
$$

A piecewise definition:

```markdown
$$
abs(x) = cases(
  x & "if" x >= 0,
  -x & "if" x < 0,
)
$$
```

$$
abs(x) = cases(
  x & "if" x >= 0,
  -x & "if" x < 0,
)
$$

The [Typst maths reference](https://typst.app/docs/reference/math/) lists every symbol and function.

## Equations that work everywhere

Without the takeover, a `{typst}` block compiles an equation to an image, and an image reaches every format:

````markdown
```{typst}
$ sum_(k=1)^n k = (n(n+1))/2 $
```
````

```{typst}
$ sum_(k=1)^n k = (n(n+1))/2 $
```

The same holds for an inline expression:

```markdown
The area is `{typst} $pi r^2$`{alt="pi r squared"} for a circle of radius r.
```

The area is `{typst} $pi r^2$`{alt="pi r squared"} for a circle of radius r.

Choose between the two by output:

- `math: typst` for HTML and Typst, where the equations stay text.
- A block or an inline expression for a document that must also produce PDF, Word, or PowerPoint.

An image carries no text, so give it an `alt` attribute for a reader who cannot see it.
